How ranking and eligibility work

AI downloads public model files from this site, then compares meaning locally. Best for English descriptions. Keyword matching works without the model.

Thematic fit and readiness are separate. The headline fit grade measures supported alignment between your description/tags and a program’s documented focus. 80–100 means Strong thematic fit; 60–79 Relevant themes; 40–59 Partial overlap; below 40 Limited overlap. A disclosed rubric combines specific shared-term evidence and local semantic similarity. It is not a probability of funding or a measured accuracy percentage. Open the fund details for the exact rubric.

Next-step badges show eligibility conflicts, questions to confirm, funding-type compatibility, application routes and timing. Missing applicant details or a closed cycle affect shortlisting, rather than lowering thematic fit. The default order prioritizes the next practical step, so it is not a simple descending sort by thematic fit. All 694 records remain available.

These are research leads, not award probabilities or eligibility approvals. Every record has a research disposition, with program terms separated from source-only overviews and unresolved checks. Sourced executable checks cover a subset of programs; other documented requirements remain manual. Geography mentions are never treated as an exhaustive eligibility list. Leadership, budgets, local boundaries and other conditions need review. Inquiry routes have their own filter and do not count as open applications.

Model: Mixedbread embed xsmall v1 (Apache 2.0), quantized and pinned. Uses a browser worker and WebAssembly, following the Artizen approach. The browser may cache public model files; project embeddings are discarded when stopped. This page blocks outbound inference connections.

    A LITTLE CONTEXT

    Useful leads.
    Honest information.

    Funding Commons makes Fito Network’s public funders directory easier to explore and organize. This research snapshot contains all 593 source records from October 14, 2026, plus 101 funders researched October 29.

    What the labels mean

    Primary research uses official funder, application and institutional sources. Other records need checking. Dates and access can change. Expired dated calls are automatically shown as closed.

    Source-only overviews help match a mission but do not confirm program terms. Unavailable or unresolved records retain directory summaries. Broad region tags do not confirm country eligibility. Amounts marked historical describe past giving. Qualitative grant bands have no assumed dollar value. Possible duplicate or related records remain separate so no source rows are lost.

    Download research coverage for all 694 records. Program reviews retain field-level official evidence; missing terms stay unknown. Each source retains its own research date. Programme prerequisites and geographic priorities were last expanded October 29, 2026.
